header.banner: Achronyme 0.1.2 is published: detached verification preserves operational errors and global JSON output

hero.subtitle: Structured host programs and zero-knowledge circuits, with explicit authority and proving trust.
hero.trustValue: Independent ceremony, public beacon, and bidirectional interoperability verified

releaseStatus.title: Published versions tied to exact source.
releaseStatus.subtitle: The installer, documentation, and playground track core 0.1.2; editor 0.3.1 remains compatible.
releaseStatus.coreDesc: Stable packages and installer artifacts are published from the core repository.
releaseStatus.editorDesc: VS Code and LSP support track the language grammar and core source revision.
releaseStatus.webDesc: The documentation and playground are deployed against the published 0.1.2 core revision.

capabilities.title: A systems language boundary around proof code.
capabilities.subtitle: The release defines how concurrent host work, external authority, circuit compilation, and cryptographic trust meet.

concurrency.title: Structured concurrency
concurrency.desc: Lexical concurrent scopes own every spawned task. Await, race, cancellation, bounded channels, and task diagnostics have explicit lifetime rules.

authority.title: Capability-scoped I/O
authority.desc: Files and TCP resources are owned values. Read, write, connect, and listen authority must be granted explicitly at the CLI or project boundary.

native.title: Interpreter, JIT, and AOT
native.desc: Run through the portable interpreter, LLVM 21 ORC JIT, or packaged native AOT runtime with visible fallback and shared runtime limits.

circuits.title: Circuit compilation
circuits.desc: Lower native Achronyme or imported Circom to optimized R1CS and witnesses, with Plonkish development paths kept visibly separate.

interop.title: Circom and snarkjs interop
interop.desc: Artik computes complex witnesses, Lysis bounds template expansion, and exported artifacts cross-check with the established snarkjs ecosystem.

trust.title: Fail-closed proving trust
trust.desc: Proof generation requires an explicit development opt-in or an immutable ceremony-derived key store bound to the exact optimized circuit.

triArch.title: Three machines, one explicit pipeline.
triArch.subtitle: Each VM owns a different responsibility instead of hiding execution, witness generation, and constraint construction behind one runtime.

akron.name: Akron
akron.desc: Runs the language, structured tasks, owned resources, closures, and proof blocks. Interpreter, JIT, and AOT share the same authority boundary.

artik.name: Artik
artik.desc: Executes deterministic witness programs, including multi-subprogram Circom lowering and native bigint operations for ECDSA-scale circuits.

lysis.name: Lysis
lysis.desc: Stages template expansion, deduplicates shared bodies, and emits constraint IR without forcing every repeated subgraph into memory at once.

featureVM.title: Concurrent host programs
featureVM.desc: Closures, collections, structured tasks, bounded channels, and owned file or TCP resources run under explicit grants and runtime limits.

featureCircuit.title: Exact circuit artifacts
featureCircuit.desc: Compile Achronyme and Circom inputs to optimized constraints and witnesses that can be checked independently with standard tooling.

featureProve.title: Proofs with an explicit key source
featureProve.desc: Proof blocks remain first-class values, but generation now fails unless development setup or a circuit-bound trusted key store is selected.

featureSolidity.title: Detached and on-chain verification
featureSolidity.desc: Export snarkjs-compatible artifacts, generate Solidity Groth16 verifiers, or verify detached BN254 and BLS12-381 proof JSON from the CLI.

proofTrust.title: Proof generation no longer invents trust for you.
proofTrust.subtitle: Achronyme separates convenient local experimentation from production proving and keeps verification independent of either key source.
proofTrust.developmentDesc: Single-party setup is available only through an explicit insecure flag. Artifacts are not production trusted.
proofTrust.productionDesc: A ceremony-derived BN254 key is packaged with its circuit hash, transcript, contribution history, and release evidence.
proofTrust.verificationDesc: Verification accepts explicit proof, public input, key, curve, and output format. It does not infer trust from project state.
proofTrust.gateDesc: The release records an independent phase-2 contribution, a precommitted public beacon, and bidirectional snarkjs interoperability against the exact release circuit.

comparison.title: Development speed without production ambiguity
comparison.subtitle: Use an explicit local setup while iterating, then switch to the exact ceremony-bound store for production.

roadmap.title: Roadmap
roadmap.subtitle: Published releases, exact source receipts, and future research are labeled separately.

now.label: 0.0.1 foundation
now.desc: Native Linux packaging, JIT, AOT, and reproducible installer artifacts.

wip.label: 0.1.2 published
wip.desc: Detached verification now preserves operational errors and applies the global JSON output contract.

next.label: After 0.1.2
next.desc: Stabilize SDK and editor distribution from measured usage.

items.multiPrimeDesc: The published 0.0.1 release provides LLVM JIT, interpreter fallback, native AOT bundles, checksums, and Linux x86_64/aarch64 production gates.
items.proveIRDesc: Proof blocks, ProveIR, R1CS export, and detached interoperability remain part of the stable product line.
items.solidityDesc: Generate Groth16 verifier contracts and export standard proof artifacts for external verification.
items.r1csOptimizerDesc: Achronyme lowers native and imported circuits through checked optimization and witness validation.
items.circomFrontendDesc: The 0.1.0 release adds lexical task scopes, bounded channels, owned resources, exact host grants, and shared interpreter/JIT/AOT semantics.
items.adversarialTestsDesc: Proof generation fails closed, production keys are circuit-bound, and independently verifiable ceremony evidence is preserved with the release.
items.playgroundDesc: The 0.3.1 editor line, playground, language reference, and release artifacts are pinned to the same core semantics.
items.multiFieldVMDesc: Turn the internal compiler and proof pipeline into a small, documented SDK only after the release contracts settle.
items.starkBackendDesc: Explore AIR and STARK backends without presenting research as a committed release.
items.noirFrontendDesc: Evaluate Noir or other frontends only where they reuse ProveIR without weakening diagnostics or trust boundaries.
items.rustSDKDesc: Expose a stable embedding API after real downstream use identifies the minimal supported surface.
items.apiFreezeDesc: Freeze the language specification, bytecode compatibility policy, and public SDK contracts.

footer.tagline: Capability-scoped programs and explicit proving trust.
